Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. 

The Brand Creative Team is evolving and elevating how the Robinhood brand shows up and reaches people – capturing attention, earning trust, and driving our next phase of growth. The next generation is figuring out their money, and we want them to do it with Robinhood. That means disruptive, culturally relevant work that cuts through where they actually spend their time and wins them over.

As Creative Director, Brand (Copy) you will lead the work that defines the brand and changes how people see Robinhood. You will concept big ideas and own them from insight to execution, with story and great writing at the core. The bar is world-class: work that breaks through, commands attention and moves the business.

This role is based in our New York, NY or Menlo Park, CA offices, with in-person attendance expected 3 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What you’ll do

  • Concept and develop big ideas that break through. Create disruptive, culturally relevant brand campaigns and moments that are unmistakably Robinhood and impossible to ignore.
  • Win the next generation. Make Robinhood a brand young investors want to hear from, talk about and trust with their money. Meet them where they live with ideas they'll actually want to be part of, not just ads they scroll past.
  • Drive results with strategy. Start with the business goal and build ideas that move the numbers. Understand how people think about money, use data to sharpen the work, and measure it by what it delivers. Our company is highly strategic, and our creatives are too.
  • Make work the world talks about. Take ideas from first insight to finished work across film, social, out-of-home, experiential, product launches and events, and refuse to let anything go out less than great. Set the pace for the category with work that gets people talking and shapes the conversation in culture.
  • Raise the bar on writing. Hold every line to a world-class standard. Build stories that stick and make people think differently about money. Set the bar for writing across the team with sharp, useful feedback for writers, designers and freelancers, and never let good enough ship.
  • Shape Robinhood's voice. Build a tone that stands out in the category, sounds like the way the next generation actually talks about money, and stays razor-sharp across every channel.
  • Direct the making. Partner with directors, production companies, artists and agencies, and stay in the work through shoot, edit and finish. Push innovation in how we make, using AI and new tools to explore more ideas faster and make better work, without diluting the brand.
  • Get everyone behind the work. Inspire leaders, partners and teams to believe in the idea and stay behind it from first pitch to launch.
  • Build with the business. Partner with Strategy, Performance Marketing, Product, Social and Design so the work is rooted in real insight and built to move the company forward. Work with Legal and Compliance early so bold ideas get cleared.

What you bring

  • 10+ years in advertising and brand creative, at a top agency, an elite in-house team, or both.
  • A portfolio of idea-led work that got made, got noticed, and moved a business, with a clear story behind each piece.
  • A copywriting background and the range to concept across film, digital, social, experiential and out-of-home.
  • Writing that is clear, distinctive and memorable, a gift for narrative, and a track record of making complex or regulated subjects feel human.
  • A record of owning and producing work end to end: working with directors and vendors, and getting ambitious ideas made on time and on budget.

What we offer

  • Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career.
  • Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching.
  • Top Tier benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents.
  • Access to the Robinhood Employee Fund that gives eligible US employees the opportunity to invest in a private employee fund that provides exposure to Robinhood Ventures funds.
  • Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not. 
  • Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more.
  • Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits.
  • Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more!

###HEADING###YOUR IMPACT

As a Family Office Advisor, you will be instrumental in shaping the financial futures of our firm's most strategic clients. You will lead and cultivate deep, enduring relationships, serving a select portfolio of 8-12 families – a client-to-advisor ratio meticulously designed to ensure dedicated attention and truly exceptional, white-glove service. For over three decades, our Advisor teams have been the trusted stewards of significant wealth, and you will continue this legacy, providing comprehensive financial planning and strategic guidance that directly impacts our clients' legacies.

###HEADING###OUR IMPACT ###HEADING###Wealth Management

Across Wealth Management, Goldman Sachs helps empower clients and customers around the world to reach their financial goals. Our advisor-led wealth management businesses provide financial planning, investment management, banking, and comprehensive advice to a wide range of clients, including ultra-high net worth and high net worth individuals, as well as family offices, foundations and endowments, and corporations and their employees. Our consumer business provides digital solutions for customers to better spend, borrow, invest, and save. Across Wealth Management, our growth is driven by a relentless focus on our people, our clients and customers, and leading-edge technology, data, and design.

Private Family Office

The Goldman Sachs Private Family Office provides financial counseling and full-service implementation to address the financial complexities of CEOs, founders, private equity principals and ultra-high net worth individuals and their families. Our clients value having a single point of contact to address their specific planning needs and manage their financial affairs. Our comprehensive approach incorporates financial planning in several areas such as consolidated investment review, income tax preparation and planning, estate planning and wealth transfer, employee benefits, risk management, philanthropic planning, and cash management.

We seek a highly accomplished and strategic professional with a proven record in ultra-high net worth wealth management.

###HEADING###HOW YOU WILL FULFILL YOUR POTENTIAL
  • Strategic Client Leadership: Function as the primary point of contact and lead advisor for a select group of ultra-high net worth families, orchestrating comprehensive financial strategies tailored to their unique needs.
  • Integrated Advisory & Coordination: Seamlessly manage and integrate advice from a network of internal and external professionals (including attorneys, accountants, and bankers) to ensure cohesive and optimal client outcomes.
  • Advanced Financial Analysis: Prepare and critically review sophisticated financial statements (balance sheets, income statements, and cash flow statements) to uncover trends, identify opportunities, and proactively address challenges.
  • Proactive Tax & Estate Planning: Develop and execute advanced tax efficiency strategies, ensuring compliance while maximizing wealth preservation. Collaborate with T&E attorneys to design and implement robust estate plans that facilitate efficient wealth transfer and minimize tax liabilities.
  • Holistic Risk Management: Design and implement comprehensive risk mitigation strategies through sophisticated insurance planning, safeguard client assets and legacies.
  • Dynamic Liquidity & Cash Flow Management: Analyze and optimize complex cash flow dynamics, ensuring robust liquidity and strategic financial positioning for our clients.
  • Impactful Philanthropic Advisory: Partner with clients to craft and implement impactful philanthropic strategies, including charitable giving and foundation planning, optimizing tax efficiency, and maximizing societal benefit.
  • Sophisticated Investment Oversight: Monitor, analyze, and report on diverse investment portfolios, including alternative investments, ensuring alignment with client objectives, and collaborating with internal and external managers to optimize performance.

SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE WE ARE LOOKING FOR

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, or a related field. An advanced degree or degree (e.g., MST, MBA, JD, CPA, CFP) is required. FINRA SIE, Series 7 and Series 66 preferred; required within 4 months of hire.
  • Experience: Minimum of 7 years of progressive experience in financial planning, tax, consulting, or a related field, with significant exposure to single or multi-family office environments. 
  • Expertise: Deep knowledge and practical application of complex financial planning concepts, including advanced tax planning, intricate estate planning, and sophisticated investment management.
  • Leadership & Influence: Demonstrated ability to manage client relationships, lead high-performing teams, and influence outcomes across a diverse stakeholder group.
  • Communication: Exceptional communication, interpersonal, and project management skills, capable of articulating complex strategies with clarity and precision.
  • Integrity: Unwavering commitment to confidentiality and the discreet handling of sensitive client information.

ABOUT GOLDMAN SACHS

At Goldman Sachs, we commit to our people, capital, and ideas to help our clients, shareholders, and the communities we serve to grow. Founded in 1869, we are a leading global investment banking, securities, and investment management firm. Headquarters in New York, we maintain offices around the world. 

We believe who you are makes you better at what you do. We are committed to fostering and advancing diversity and inclusion in our own workplace and beyond by ensuring every individual within our firm has a number of opportunities to grow professionally and personally, from our training and development opportunities and firmwide networks to benefits, wellness and personal finance offerings and mindfulness programs. Learn more about our culture, benefits, and people at GS.com/careers. 

We are committed to finding reasonable accommodation for candidates with special needs or disabilities during our recruitment process. Learn more: https://www.goldmansachs.com/careers/footer/disability-statement.html

descriptions.job-0ywybo4:
Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

You will open doors at the North American private-sector financial institutions and crypto businesses TRM most needs in its network, so that senior conversations turn into the first qualified opportunity for an Account Director.

This is a senior individual contributor role in the Strategic Accounts team, built around a network you have already earned rather than a closing quota. You hand each opportunity to the Account Director at demo and step back after trial, with AI doing the account research and pipeline upkeep so your time goes to the conversations only you can have.

The impact you will have:

  • Your relationships decide which North American financial institutions TRM reaches this year: you turn a senior network into first meetings, using AI research agents to prepare each account's structure, recent news, regulatory posture, and likely stakeholders before the first conversation.

  • TRM stays in the room when a champion leaves, because you build relationships across compliance, investigations, risk, and digital asset teams, and use AI to map stakeholders and flag coverage gaps in each named account.

  • You create the first qualified opportunity in accounts that standard coverage has not cracked, and hand it to the Account Director at demo with an AI-assisted account brief, so the AD starts from context.

  • TRM earns a seat at conferences, panels, and practitioner forums through your voice, and you use AI to turn event overlap and hallway conversations into tracked follow-ups within days.

  • Pipeline data stays current without manual upkeep: you use AI workflows across Salesforce and Gong notes to log activity and surface patterns across your network, such as recurring objections and rising interest.

  • What you hear in the field reaches Product, Marketing, and Policy quickly, because you summarize market and regulatory signal with AI and share it as short, structured notes.

What we’re looking for:

  • A deep, credible network across North American financial institutions or crypto infrastructure firms, ideally as a former head of digital assets at a bank or a senior BD owner at a custody or settlement provider, with AI-assisted tools to keep that network mapped and current.

  • A track record of turning relationships into real, trackable pipeline, not only warm introductions, with clean Salesforce records kept through AI-assisted logging.

  • Comfort as a public voice for TRM at conferences, panels, and practitioner forums, with AI-assisted prep for talking points and follow-up.

  • A concrete, repeatable AI workflow you can walk through, such as a real account where AI research changed how you approached the conversation.

  • Experience building senior relationships across several functions in one account, and using AI to keep stakeholder maps current.

  • Based in the United States (NYC preferred), willing to travel 30-40% for conferences and in-person account work, and comfortable using AI tools every week to plan travel and prepare each meeting.

About the Team:

  • You join Elias Kokaly's Strategic Accounts team, a small, senior group focused on unlocking TRM's hardest named accounts.

  • The BDE function is growing by region and segment, so you will have peers opening doors in other markets and a shared playbook to improve together.

  • The work is intellectually demanding: the people you meet are senior, the buying groups are large, and your credibility has to hold up in every conversation.

  • You collaborate closely with Account Directors, Pathfinders, Product, and Marketing, and you share what works so the whole team benefits.

Team Operating Rhythms:

  • Distributed, not distant: the team works across time zones. Your time zone is United States based (NYC preferred), with overlap hours to be confirmed by the hiring manager.

  • Communication is written first: clear, brief updates in Slack and Salesforce, with live time reserved for account strategy and customer conversations.

  • Regular account reviews with the hiring manager and the regional sales head decide which doors to open next, with cadence to be confirmed at intake.

  • Handoffs are explicit: opportunities move to the Account Director at demo, and the BDE steps back after trial, with no account splits or quota overlap.

Travel Requirements:

  • Schedule: 30-40% travel for conferences and in-person account work.

Learn about TRM Speed in this position:

  • Within 30 days, a mapped list of named North American accounts and the senior relationships you can activate, so first outreach starts in week two instead of month two.

  • Within 60 days, the first senior meetings booked inside strategic accounts that coverage has not reached, each with an AI-prepared stakeholder map and a clear next step.

  • Within 90 days, the first BDE-sourced opportunity handed to an Account Director at demo with a complete account brief, so the AD can book a trial without repeating discovery.

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

  • Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

  • Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly

  • Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.

Privacy Policy and Additional Information

By submitting your application, you agree to allow TRM Labs to process your personal information in accordance with our Privacy Policy.

We collect the information you provide (such as your resume, work history, and contact details) solely for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for current and future roles at TRM.

Because our hiring cycles for certain positions may span 24 to 36 months, we retain your personal information for up to 36 months from the date of your application. After that period, your data is deleted unless a different retention period is required or permitted by law.

If you are located in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or another jurisdiction with applicable data protection laws, you have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of your personal data at any time before that period ends. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at privacy@trmlabs.com.

To notify TRM Labs that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance.

The use of AI tools of any kind (including but not limited to notetakers, interview assistants, and real-time coaching tools such as Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom, Cluey, or similar) during TRM interviews is not permitted without prior approval from TRM. TRM uses its own internal tools for note-taking to ensure a consistent and confidential experience for all candidates.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this form.

Recruitment agencies

TRM Labs does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to TRM employees. TRM Labs is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company without a signed agreement.

dtcpay is a MAS licensed payment service provider that bridges traditional finance and digital assets. We enable businesses to accept and make payments in both fiat and digital currencies, delivering secure, efficient, and seamless payment experiences across borders. As we expand globally, we are shaping the future of digital payments.   • Gather relevant information, identify the appropriate engineering team, and coordinate issue resolution until closure.

About Sapiom

Sapiom is building payment infrastructure for AI agents. We enable agents to make purchases for people, manage payments between businesses, and buy the compute, inference, and APIs they need to operate. As agents become part of everyday life, we're building toward the experiences people will use to trust them with their money: one place to set what agents can do, see what they did, and stay in control across every agent they use.

Through one integration, Sapiom connects agents to funding sources and payment methods. Our intent verification checks that each transaction matches what the person or business authorized. Spending controls define where and how much agents can spend, with a record of every transaction and its outcome. We're building toward a world where people and businesses can delegate payments to agents with confidence.

We're a small team in San Francisco with deep experience in payments and infrastructure. Our founder was Director of Engineering in Payments at Shopify for five years. We've raised $50 million in our first 12 months from Accel, Dragonfly, Coinbase Ventures, Okta Ventures, Menlo Ventures and Anthropic.

About the role

Agents are starting to act and transact on their own. For that to work, people have to trust them, and most of that trust is won or lost in the experience. This is a chance to define what design means in a new era: the experiences that make the agentic economy work for people haven't been invented yet. You'll design for developers building on Sapiom today, and help shape consumer experiences that put people in control of the agents acting for them.

For now, you'll be our only designer. You'll own how Sapiom looks and works, working closely with our founder, product and engineering: deciding what design needs to happen, taking problems from a rough idea to shipped product, and setting the standard for design across the company. This is a high-autonomy, Staff-level role. The right person is a systems thinker who's fluent in how AI agents work, uses AI to explore and build at a speed that wasn't possible before, and has the taste to separate great work from generic output.

What you will do

Own the end-to-end design process across Sapiom's product: from early discovery and requirements gathering with Product, through iterative visual design, to guiding implementation with Engineering. You'll work on the hardest UX problems in agentic commerce, where there's no playbook yet, and make autonomous activity clear and trustworthy to the people behind it.

You’ll also help define Sapiom’s design language and how our brand shows up in the market. Product comes first. The goal: software that earns developer trust on first use and deepens it every time.

  • Own the full design process across product surfaces. Run design from early workshops and mockups to production-quality prototypes, delivering the right artifact at the right moment. Use AI to explore far more directions, prototype in code and automate the busywork, so your time goes to craft.

  • Ship interfaces for problems no one has solved before, across developer tools, consumer experiences and the conversations people have with agents.

  • Design the moments where people decide to trust an agent, so they feel safe at a glance wherever they appear, including inside a partner's product.

  • Build and maintain Sapiom's design system, and keep it consistent between Figma and code with an eye towards knowing when convention serves users and when a new pattern is necessary.

  • Set the bar for design quality across the company by establishing shared standards and giving and asking for feedback with candor.

  • Own Sapiom’s visual identity and support brand and marketing design when needed, so we become known for our design.

You've worked at Staff level, thinking in systems, not just screens, and taking big swings to raise the quality of what shipped.

Your portfolio shows real products and the tradeoffs behind them, not just final screens. BitGo maintains a global presence and multiple regulated entities, including BitGo Bank & Trust, National Association, the first federally chartered digital asset trust bank owned by a publicly traded company. This role will require being full-time onsite at our New York, NY office to support collaborative team dynamics and innovative problem-solving.

BitGo is looking for a design leader who still designs. You will manage and mentor the design team, own the design system, and sit next to the Chief Product Officer on business strategy.

This is a player-coach role, and we mean it literally. You will carry your own design surfaces and ship them, alongside leading the team. Expect roughly 50% hands-on IC work to start, decreasing as the team scales. It will not go to zero — the person setting the craft bar should be practicing at it.

We are not a design-forward company today. We intend to become one, and we want you to lead that shift.

The team you will lead

The design team is small, senior, and self-sufficient. Each designer owns a wide vertical outright — trading, staking, DeFi vaults, earn, wallets, financing — with deep product context and strong opinions about the work. They are running at capacity, which is part of why this role carries real IC load: you will pick up the retail mobile experience and design system rather than distributing that work across a team that is already full.

What they have asked for is specific, and we are hiring against it: a leader who gets into the work early with product and engineering rather than arriving at the end, who can critique craft because they still practice it, who tells them plainly what the next level requires, and who gives the team air cover so they can do the deep work instead of patching to hit dates.

What you will own

  • Your own design work. You will own surfaces directly and ship them at the quality bar you are asking of everyone else. Discovery through spec, in Figma, in the reviews, on the hard problems.
  • The team's growth. Invest in each designer individually. Be explicit about what the next level requires and give people the work that gets them there. Feedback should be candid, specific, and about the craft. Respect the ownership designers already have — autonomy is how this team works best, and your job is to raise the ceiling, not take the pen.
  • Design's standing in the company. Amplify the team's visibility, voice, and strategic impact. Represent design in strategy, roadmap, and architecture conversations, and push for the client experience when nobody else in the room will.
  • Upstream involvement. Join product and engineering at discovery, not at handoff. Shape long-term roadmaps with PMs so the team builds toward a direction instead of absorbing late changes.
  • The design system. Own the system and component library end to end: tokens, patterns, governance, contribution model, and adoption across product teams. Translate company strategy into a system flexible enough that teams ship scalable experiences rather than one-off patches.
  • Systems design. Our platform spans seven product areas with shared primitives — accounts, wallets, assets, entitlements, approvals. Design the system, not the screen.
  • The discipline. Establish UX and systems thinking as a practice the whole organization runs on, not a stage a design team owns. Product managers, engineers, and business leads should be able to frame a client problem, map the system it lives in, and evaluate a solution against real client needs. That is how we ship value to every client type we serve, in every market we operate in — rather than a set of features that work for the loudest account.
  • How we work. Establish the processes a small team needs to move fast without losing quality: critique, documentation, design review, and clean handoffs with engineering. Set the quality bar and hold it, including for AI-assisted work.
  • Technical depth. Read a technical design, understand the constraint, and decide with engineering where to compromise, where to hold, and where a broader change is worth the cost. Get into the mechanics with the team on the hard edge cases — the crypto ones and the design ones.
  • The face of design. Be present and known internally, and represent BitGo design externally with clients, partners, and candidates.

What success looks like

By six months: the design system has a clear owner, a versioned component library, and measurable adoption. Product teams stop reinventing patterns. You have shipped design work of your own that the team points to as the standard. Every designer knows what their next level requires and has work that supports getting there.

By 12 months: design is in the room early on strategy, not late on execution. Product and engineering partners frame problems in client terms without being asked. The team has grown in size and capability. At least one flagship surface has shipped with a coherent, systemized experience clients notice.

Who you are

  • Experience leading design in financial services. Digital assets, or another domain of genuinely complex technical flows, strongly preferred.
  • You have built and owned a design system at scale, not just used one.
  • Hands-on in Figma and a role model for craft. You are shipping design work today, not describing work you shipped four years ago. You can sit in a critique and give feedback that is specific enough to act on.
  • Deep in UX. Strong product thinking, logical reasoning, and decisions grounded in data rather than taste alone.
  • You have managed designers and made them better. You care about how the team is doing, not only what it ships.
  • Technically literate. Comfortable with APIs, data models, and engineering trade-offs.
  • Direct communicator. You can hold a position with a Chief Product Officer, an engineering lead, or a client, and change your mind when the argument is better.
  • You want the mandate. Turning a technical, compliance-heavy platform into a design-led one is the appeal, not the obstacle.

Helpful, not required

  • Regulated environments: broker-dealer, trust company, bank, or qualified custodian.
  • Experience with complex permissioning, approval workflows, or multi-entity account structures.
  • Design leadership at a company that went through the same shift you would lead here.

Why Join BitGo?

Disrupting an industry takes vision, innovation, passion, technical chops, drive to deliver, collaboration, and execution. Join a team of great people who strive for excellence and personify our corporate values of ownership, craftsmanship, and open communication. We are looking for new colleagues who bring innovative ways of thinking and problem-solving, and who want risks to be part of the team that changes the world’s financial markets.

  • 100% company-paid health insurance for employee, partner, and dependents
  • Up to 4% 401k company match

  • Free commuter/parking pass
  • Free custom lunches and snacks
  • Computer equipment and workplace furniture to suit your needs
  • Great colleagues and an inspiring environment

Benefits may vary based on location.

Pay Transparency Notice:

Depending upon your leveling and location, the compensation for this role averages between $210,000 and $250,000 USD base salary. Equity, an annual performance bonus, and the benefits outlined above are also part of this role’s package.

Cryptocurrencies are the most disruptive change the financial services industry has seen in years. Join us and you'll be able to look back and say you were part of the team that transformed investing.

We are a diverse team of free thinkers, and fast movers united to help investors and creators energize the global economy. Who You Are

You are a controls and OT network engineer who has seen what happens when the network is treated as an afterthought, and you want a seat at the table when the decisions are actually made. You have built and supported networks that could not be allowed to fail, and you are ready to move upstream to the owner’s side of a large capital program, where one early call gets locked into drawings, procurement, and a GMP. You hold a position with conviction and change it when the evidence says so. You can walk a design firm through a markup, walk a finance partner through a cost tradeoff, and do both in the same afternoon

What You’ll Do:

Every Galaxy campus depends on a controls network that ties cooling, electrical, and monitoring systems together, and it has to behave the same way at the next site as it does at the last one. As Data Center Controls Network Engineer, you will sit within Galaxy’s Pre-Construction team and act as the owner’s technical voice on OT networking, from the point a site is acquired through GMP handoff to construction. You will begin with the Helios campus in Texas and carry what you learn into the sites that follow, working with Galaxy’s pre-construction, design and engineering, construction, and operations groups and with the design firms, integrators, and suppliers they engage. Key Responsibilities

  • Set the Owner’s Position: Turn tenant, power, and cooling requirements into a written OT network position that design firms and the general contractor can build from, so key decisions are made once and made early.
  • Build the Galaxy Playbook: Create the standards, typical details, and repeatable design packages that let each new campus start from what worked on the last one.

  • Draw the Line Between OT and IT: Agree on the boundary between the OT and corporate networks, remote access for vendors and tenants, and firewall rules with Galaxy IT and security before the design is frozen.
  • Make Testing Contractual: Build acceptance criteria and test requirements for factory, site, failover, and integrated systems testing into scopes and commissioning plans, so proof of performance is a contract requirement rather than a favor.
  • Vet Equipment Early: Check submittals, firmware selections, and baseline configurations against Galaxy standards, and catch mismatches in the office instead of in the field.
  • Plan for the Operators: Write down what operations will have to live with, including change control, configuration backups, firmware management, monitoring, and rollback procedures, before the design is final.
  • Put Numbers on It: Give technical input to budgets, GMP pricing review, and schedule for controls and network scope, and surface cost, schedule, and value-engineering effects as early as possible.
  • Pass the Baton: Deliver the design basis, open items, and lessons learned to construction and commissioning teams, and stay available to them through early construction.

  • Experience developing RFQs and RFPs, leveling bids, or selecting vendors for technical scopes.
  • Working knowledge of delivery models such as GMP and of how design decisions drive cost and schedule.

  • Experience supporting multiple sites or campuses and keeping them consistent with one another.

Who we are

About Stripe

About the team

Abuse Control Engineering (ACE) is Stripe’s rapid-response technical defense and control incubator. When urgent abuse vectors emerge, ACE uses real-world attacker telemetry to prototype, test, and deploy software safeguards before vulnerabilities can be exploited at scale.

We partner closely with Fraud, Risk, Abuse Research, and Product Engineering to run rigorous experiments that balance effective risk mitigation with legitimate user activity and conversion. Operating as both a strike team and an incubator, ACE builds automated regression suites to prevent threats from recurring and transfers mature controls to long-term product owners across Stripe.

What you’ll do

As an Abuse Control Engineer on the ACE team, you will design, prototype, and incubate technical defenses that safeguard Stripe’s financial ecosystem against complex, cross-cutting abuse vectors.

When emerging threat patterns reveal weaknesses in Stripe products, ACE rapidly builds and experiments with technical safeguards. Guided by empirical evidence and Stripe’s Fraud Taxonomy 3.0 (FT3) framework, you will translate threat intelligence into precise technical control requirements, such as API rate limits, step-up challenges, parameter validation, and pre-debit holds.

You will run experiments to evaluate risk reduction against the impact on legitimate user conversion, carefully balancing security and product velocity. You will manage controls through a structured incubation lifecycle, build automated regression suites to prevent threats from recurring, and partner with product engineering teams to transfer mature, long-term defenses.

Responsibilities

  • Rapid control prototyping: Design, prototype, and deploy technical controls across API, protocol, and product boundaries to address high-impact abuse vectors.
  • Evidence-based technical requirements: Translate empirical attacker evidence and FT3 threat research from Abuse Research, Fraud, and Security teams into precise technical abuse requirements and control specifications.
  • Control co-design: Collaborate with teams across Stripe to design resilient, secure controls across payments, onboarding, identity, and Connect surfaces.
  • Risk experimentation: Run rigorous experiments and A/B tests to measure risk reduction against the impact on legitimate user conversion, optimizing controls to minimize friction while neutralizing threats.
  • Regression testing: Build comprehensive regression test suites and automated attack simulations with Abuse Research to ensure mitigated abuse vectors do not recur.
  • Stakeholder management: Execute ACE’s incubation model by defining handoff criteria, operational documentation, timelines, and target dates for transferring successful controls to product teams.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 10+ years of experience in security engineering, software engineering, application security, or anti-abuse engineering in a high-scale production environment.
  • A bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, cybersecurity, software engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • A strong software development background, with proficiency in Python, Go, Java, or a similar production programming language, as well as advanced SQL skills for analyzing system telemetry.
  • Experience using frontier AI models for software development, learning, and analysis.
  • Hands-on experience building API-level safeguards, rate-limiting frameworks, authentication or authorization checks, or input-validation controls.
  • Experience with automated testing frameworks, including writing unit, integration, and regression tests for critical backend software.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration and communication skills, with a track record of partnering across security, product, and platform teams to drive technical outcomes.

Preferred qualifications

  • A track record of designing and executing A/B tests, evaluating control efficacy, and balancing security safeguards against user conversion friction.
  • Expertise in threat modeling, secure systems architecture, and modern application-security design principles.
  • Familiarity with established threat frameworks, such as FT3 or MITRE ATT&CK, and experience applying adversary kill-chain analysis to build resilient defenses.
  • Knowledge of financial fraud vectors, threat-actor tactics, techniques, and procedures, and attacker infrastructure, including account takeover, card testing, and credential stuffing.
  • Hands-on experience with large-scale data-processing platforms, such as Databricks, Trino, or PySpark, to monitor and measure control performance across distributed systems.
  • Experience incubating software features, establishing clear operational handoff criteria, and transitioning ownership to partner engineering teams.

The role & why it matters 

We are looking for someone to take ownership of Transaction Monitoring at BCB and shape its next stage. You will run the function day to day, leading a globally dispersed team of over 10 analysts and senior analysts, set the standard for what good looks like, and deliver it: refine rules so they focus on real risk, extend coverage as our products grow, automate manual, low-judgement work, and build a team that investigates well and escalates with confidence. You report to the Head of Financial Crime Operations and you will have real authority over how transaction monitoring works across fiat and crypto, as the first line of defence for the Group.

This is a role for someone who sees a process that could work better and improves it without waiting to be asked.

BCB moves fiat and digital assets 24/7 for some of the largest crypto businesses in the world, through our Client Console, API and BLINC instant settlement network. Monitoring has to keep pace with that volume and speed. We have solid foundations, and we want a leader who will build on them to create a function that is data-led, well documented, measurable and increasingly automated, and that keeps alert and case volumes under control as the business grows.

What you will own

  • The transaction monitoring framework for fiat and crypto across the Group, including rules, scenarios, thresholds, typologies and the documented rationale behind each.
  • Confirm every product, entity and payment flow feeds the monitoring system completely and accurately, including new products before launch.
  • Alert handling end to end: triage, investigation, escalation, case management and closure, with clear SLAs and quality standards, covering transaction monitoring alerts, sanctions and PEP screening hits on customers and counterparties.
  • Backlog and capacity: keep alert and case queues within tolerance, plan rotas and capacity against volume growth, and step in quickly when backlogs build.
  • Oversight of any outsourced or third-party review capacity, including SLA performance, quality and escalation standards.
  • Decisions to escalate internal suspicious activity reports (ISARs) to the MLRO, and the quality of those reports: well reasoned, evidenced and on time, and support to the MLRO in preparing external SARs/STRs, including to the NCA, TRACFIN and FINTRAC. 
  • Rule calibration tuning and effectiveness testing, using data to cut false positives and find the activity current rules miss. Document rationale behind each, with changes approved through BCB’s governance process in partnership with Compliance (2LOD) and the MLRO.
  • Automation of manual, low-judgement, work, whether through vendor tooling, workflow automation, scripting or AI-assisted review.
  • Blockchain analytics as part of monitoring, not a separate step.
  • A quality assurance and quality control framework for the team, with sampling, feedback loops and results reported to governance.
  • Management information for senior leadership and governance forums: volumes, backlog, ageing, conversion rates, quality results, emerging risk.
  • Procedures (SOPs) for the function, kept current and usable by the people doing the work.
  • Leadership of the TM team of over 10 people, working through senior analysts: team structure, hiring, coaching, and performance, and building senior analysts who can make day-to-day decisions without you. Building a robust operating model that increasingly relies upon efficiency, automated workflows and AI over increased headcount.
  • Working relationships with Compliance, Onboarding, Fraud, Product, Engineering and Data, and with regulators and auditors when they review the function. Represent transaction monitoring at governance forums and deputise for the Head of Financial Crime Operations on monitoring matters. 

What success looks like

First 30 days. Review the current rules, alert volumes, backlog, team structure and procedures. Meet the team and key stakeholders. Present a written assessment of what works, what does not and what you will change first, with a sequenced plan and a view on capacity and resourcing .

First 90 days. Any backlog is cleared or on a committed recovery plan. Alerts are consistently worked within SLA. Rules have been reviewed and tuned, with documented rationale for each change and governance approval for each change. At least two manual processes are automated. MI is produced to a regular cadence for senior leadership to review. Every team member has clear objectives and a development plan.

First 3-6 months. Monitoring coverage maps to BCB's risk assessment and product set, including new products before launch. False positive rates are measurably lower with no loss of detection, and investigations are faster. QC and QA results consistently meet targets. The function would pass an internal audit or regulatory review without material findings, and the team runs well without you in every decision, senior analysts own day-to-day case decisions and you have a credible deputy in your absence.

What you bring

  • Five or more years in transaction monitoring or financial crime investigations, with at least two in a lead or management role.
  • Experience in payments, e-money, banking or crypto. Experience across both fiat and crypto is a strong advantage.
  • A track record of improving a monitoring function: you can describe a rule set you rebuilt, a backlog you cleared or a process you automated, and the numbers before and after.
  • Experience of workforce and capacity planning, QA/QC frameworks and managing operational SLAs, including oversight of outsourced review capacity. 
  • Hands-on knowledge of rule design, threshold calibration and effectiveness testing.
  • Sound judgement on suspicion and SAR decisions, and the ability to teach that judgement to others.
  • Working knowledge of UK AML requirements, including the MLRs and JMLSG guidance, and of sanctions regimes (UK, EU, OFAC, UN) and PEP screening. Some exposure to EU requirements. Experience of France’s ACPR or AMF and reporting to TRACFIN, reporting to FINTRAC in Canada and an understanding of the FIU reporting regimes in UAE and Switzerland is an advantage.
  • Comfort with data. You can query it, interpret it and make decisions from it. SQL or Python is a plus.
  • Experience with blockchain analytics tools such as Chainalysis, Elliptic or TRM.
  • A clear view on where automation and AI help in monitoring, and where they need human oversight.
  • Clear and precise written English. Your case notes, SOPs and MI are easy to follow and hard to misread.

How you work

You are direct and decisive. You make a call, explain it and own the outcome. You question rules and processes that exist only because they always have. You prefer fixing root causes over adding headcount. Can produce MI such as cost per alert and capacity forecasting against volume growth. You build trust with the team by being in the detail with them, and with senior stakeholders by telling them plainly what the risk is. You develop your senior analysts so decisions do not all route through you.

About the Opportunity

The VIP Growth Manager will serve as a central strategy and operations partner for the VIP business. Through data analysis, user insights, and cross-functional collaboration, this role will support VIP Relationship Managers and regional teams with growth strategies and initiatives.
The ideal candidate should possess strong analytical thinking and communication skills, with the ability to identify growth opportunities from user behavior and business data, translate insights into actionable plans, and collaborate with relevant teams to drive execution and continuous optimization.

Business Insights & Strategy
  • Identify structural problems and opportunities in the data, such as churn signals among high-value users, differences in service needs across client segments, and the marginal return on resource allocation, and turn them into actionable strategies.

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Specialist Solutions Architects (SSAs) are domain experts aligned to Stripe’s solutions and the customer buying centers they serve. We combine deep product and industry expertise with an understanding of our customers’ most complex business and technical challenges.

The SSA team partners with specialist sellers and the broader pre-sales organization to shape strategic opportunities, develop pipeline, improve revenue attainment, and turn Stripe’s product capabilities into measurable customer outcomes. We also bring field insights to Product and Engineering, helping influence Stripe’s roadmap and go-to-market strategy.

Stripe's Revenue Suite helps businesses monetize however their customers want to buy: subscription, usage-based, or hybrid pricing. As monetization models get more complex and pricing becomes something companies iterate on continuously rather than set once, this team sits at the center of how Stripe helps businesses price, bill, recognize, and report on revenue.

What you’ll do

As Global Head of Specialist Solutions Architecture for Revenue, you will lead the global strategy, execution, and growth of the SSA organization supporting Stripe's full Revenue Suite: Stripe Billing and Metronome together. You will define how Stripe engages customers across the entire monetization-to-revenue-reporting lifecycle, including subscription management, usage-based and hybrid billing, invoicing, tax, revenue recognition, and analytics, from initial business and technical discovery through solution design, adoption, value realization, and expansion.

This is a second line leadership role. You will manage a mix of regional managers, each leading their own team of specialist architects, along with a small number of senior individual contributors reporting to you directly. You will build and develop this multi-layered organization and create the operating model, playbooks, and cross-functional partnerships needed to scale it worldwide. Working closely with Sales, Marketing, Alliances, Professional Services, Support, Product, and Engineering, you will help customers modernize their revenue infrastructure while accelerating adoption and growth for Stripe's Revenue Suite across every region we operate in.

This is an opportunity to shape a global function at an important point in Stripe's expansion beyond payments. You will connect deep technical expertise to customer value and commercial outcomes while ensuring that customer needs from every region influence Stripe's global product and go-to-market direction.

Responsibilities

  • Own and execute the global technical sales strategy for Stripe's Revenue Suite, aligning specialist coverage, priorities, and investments with growth opportunities across AMER, EMEA, and APAC
  • Recruit, lead, and develop a high-performing organization of regional managers and senior individual contributors, establishing clear expectations for technical excellence, customer impact, and commercial contribution
  • Coach and develop your managers directly, building their leadership capability so they can in turn grow strong specialist architects on their own teams
  • Partner with Sales leadership to prioritize resources, shape account strategies, and improve the progression and conversion of complex opportunities
  • Establish repeatable engagement models, playbooks, reference architectures, and execution standards across the monetization-to-revenue-reporting lifecycle, including subscription management, usage-based and hybrid billing, invoicing, tax, revenue recognition, and analytics
  • Advise executives, developers, architects, finance leaders, and other decision-makers on modernizing their monetization and revenue-management architectures
  • Guide strategic customers from business and technical discovery through solution design, validation, adoption, value realization, and expansion
  • Translate recurring customer needs, market signals, and deal friction into actionable insights that influence Product and Engineering priorities
  • Represent the Revenue SSA organization in global leadership forums, providing clear perspectives on performance, capacity, risks, customer needs, and growth opportunities
  • Shape the Revenue Suite go-to-market approach across every region, accounting for regional regulatory requirements, business models, and market-specific billing practices
  • Build strong collaboration and knowledge-sharing mechanisms across regional and global teams to improve consistency, reuse, and execution quality
  • Advance Stripe's external thought leadership through executive briefings, industry events, white papers, and reference architectures focused on billing, monetization, tax automation, and revenue management

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 15+ years of experience in technical sales, solutions architecture, solution consulting, or another customer-facing technical role in enterprise technology
  • 10+ years of experience building and scaling pre-sales or solutions architecture teams, including hiring, managing, coaching, and developing senior individual contributors 
  • Experience managing managers, with a track record of developing people leaders and running a multi-layered organization
  • Demonstrated success partnering with sales leaders on complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise opportunities and connecting technical strategy to commercial outcomes
  • Deep understanding of modern monetization models, including subscription, usage-based, and hybrid pricing, and how businesses increasingly treat pricing as something to iterate on continuously rather than set once, and how that shapes billing, invoicing, and revenue-management requirements
  • Strong technical background with a solid understanding of APIs, distributed systems, and modern software development practices
  • Experience operating across global markets, with an ability to adapt leadership and go-to-market approaches across different regions and cultures
  • Strong executive communication, relationship-building, and cross-functional leadership skills
  • Ability to communicate complex business and technical concepts clearly to audiences ranging from developers and architects to finance leaders and C-level executives
  • Willingness to travel up to 30% of the time

Preferred qualifications

  • Working knowledge of the full revenue management lifecycle: recurring and usage-based billing, subscription management, invoicing, tax automation (sales tax and VAT), revenue recognition, financial/custom reporting, and the data pipelines that feed them
  • Experience designing or advising on complex enterprise architectures and integrations involving financial or revenue-management systems, including configure-price-quote, order-to-cash, revenue recognition, and ERP systems
  • Experience with usage-based or consumption billing platforms and the metering, pricing, and invoicing architectures they require
  • Experience building or scaling a global technical go-to-market function during a period of rapid product or organizational growth
  • A track record of translating field insights into meaningful product, engineering, or go-to-market changes
  • Experience developing executive-facing thought leadership, reference architectures, or industry-specific solution strategies
  • Familiarity with the regulatory and commercial considerations that affect billing, tax, and revenue management across AMER, EMEA, and APAC
